claim: Age-related macular degeneration (AMD) is the leading cause of irreversible blindness among the elderly in the Western world.
source: Age-related macular degeneration (AMD) is the leading cause of irreversible blindness among the elderly in the Western world (Friedman et al., 2004; Resnikoff et al., 2004; Singer et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to three published studies (Friedman et al., 2004; Resnikoff et al., 2004; Singer et al., 2012).

claim: Atrophic AMD is characterized by the progressive loss of retinal pigment epithelial (RPE) cells and photoreceptor cells.
source: Atrophic AMD (aAMD, also known as 'dry' AMD) is characterized by the progressive loss of retinal pigment epithelial (RPE) cells and photoreceptor cells, which can coalesce and cause geographic atrophy in the macular region.
evidence: This is a descriptive statement about the characteristics of atrophic AMD, drawing from established scientific knowledge about the disease.

claim: Neovascular AMD is characterized by choroidal neovascularization (CNV).

claim: Anti-VEGF compounds are used to treat nvAMD by reducing leakage and the progression of CNV.

evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a published study (Rosenfeld et al., 2006).
